Serve a run's model with Ollama

Source: R/serve.R
dragon_serve_ollama.Rd

Merges the adapter into the base model (if not done already), registers the result with Ollama, and checks that Ollama can answer with it. The returned backend points dragon_generate() and dragon_chat() at it.

Usage

dragon_serve_ollama(
  run,
  name = NULL,
  quantize = NULL,
  ollama = ollama_path(),
  llama_cpp_dir = Sys.getenv("LLAMA_CPP_DIR", unset = "")
)

Arguments

run

A dragon_run, or a merged model directory.

name

Model name to register. Defaults to dragonfarm-<run id>.

quantize

Optional quantization such as "q8_0" to shrink the served model. On the GGUF route it is the converter's output type (default "q8_0").

ollama

Path to the ollama executable.

llama_cpp_dir

A llama.cpp checkout; when it holds the converter, the GGUF route is used.

Value

A dragon_backend for the served model.

Details

With a llama.cpp checkout (LLAMA_CPP_DIR), the merged model is first converted to GGUF with dragon_export_gguf() and Ollama serves that file; this worked with Ollama 0.40.5 on Windows. Without one, Ollama is asked to import the safetensors directly. Recent Ollama versions do that through their MLX engine, which on Windows refused a Qwen run and could not run a SmolLM2 one ("MLX runtime is not available"); the unusable copy is then removed and the error says so.

Needs Ollama installed and its service running. The ollama command is looked for on the PATH and then in Ollama's usual install folders.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
backend <- dragon_serve_ollama(run)
options(dragonfarm.backend = backend)
dragon_chat(run)$say("Hello")
}
